studies a text and identifies verb conjugations in level 7-9.

practicals.title: Drawing Organogram
practicals.description_verbatim: draw an organogram for any political or traditional institution.

suggested_uses: use computer animations to demonstrate electoral processes.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates individual rights.
learning_outcomes: state the fundamental human rights (k).
explain forms of human rights abuses, organs and organisations that are supposed to protect human rights (k, u).
know and use noun classes 15-18 (where applicable) (k, u).
know children’s rights/ responsibilities and organs and institutions that protect human rights (k, v, a).
know workers’ rights and organs and institutions that protect workers’ rights and how workers benefit from labour laws (k, u).
know the rights of people with disabilities (PWDs) and organs and institutions that protect their rights (k, u).
know how words are reduplicated (where applicable) (k, u).

suggested_learning_activities.description: teacher guides learners to brainstorm and clarifies the meaning of ‘fundamental human rights’.
learners study a text on human rights and identify examples of fundamental human rights.
learners present their findings on fundamental human rights and teacher clarifies on key issues or provides further examples.
learners brainstorm on the meaning of human rights abuses and relevant organs, organisations and persons responsible for tackling such abuses.
learners share personal experiences or examples of human rights abuses they know of.
teacher provides learners with a sample text on human rights abuses and learners identify ways in which basic human rights can be violated.
using relevant examples, teacher guides learners to recollect prior knowledge of noun classes previously learnt.
using the above example, teacher introduces noun classes 15-18 with concrete examples on a board or chart.
learners use teacher’s example to generate at least five examples of nouns in classes 15-18.
using prior knowledge on human rights, learners brainstorm or suggest examples of children’s rights and responsibilities.
teacher guides learners to identify institutions/organisations that promote human rights.
teacher appreciates learner’s contribution and makes further clarification on children’s rights and responsibilities clearly differentiating the two concepts.
teacher asks learners to share their experiences on whether they have been employers or employees and what rights they had or owed their employees.
based on prior knowledge on human rights, learners brainstorm examples of workers’ rights.
learners study a text on safety regulations for a workplace and explain in groups how these regulations protect or promote workers’ rights.
teacher explains the meaning of pwds and asks learners to suggest suitable examples.
learners listen to a presentation from a human right’s expert on pwds and a compile a list of rights of pwds.
in groups, learners write a one-page report on rights of pwds that are often ignored/abused suggesting ways in which these rights can be promoted.
in groups, learners conduct a study in their school or community on pwds and write a report on how their rights have been abused and promoted.
with relevant examples, teacher explains the concept of reduplication and its purpose in speech or writing.
learners study a text and identify reduplicated words.
learners identify more examples of verbs, adverbs and adjectives and demonstrate how they can be reduplicated.
learners use reduplicated words to construct sentences orally or in writing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: discusses in groups children’s rights and responsibilities.
writes placards for pwds.
debates on the topic: workers’ rights should be abolished.
reads and responds orally to a two-page text on human rights violation and protection.
carries out a paper/internet research into abuses of the rights of pwds.
in groups, reduplicates at least five verbs, adverbs and adjectives.
studies a text and identifies reduplicated verbs, adverbs and adjectives.
listens and gives speeches on human rights.

assessment_weightings.notes_verbatim: This summative teacher assessment will contribute 20% to the final grade of the School Leaving Certificate as elaborated in the Assessment Framework.

suggested_uses: use the Internet as a source of information about human rights.
use a computer to type a report on human rights abuse.
use a computer to design a poster to raise awareness against a vulnerable group of people.
